explanation: The Romans invaded Britain in AD 43 under Claudius, built roads and towns, never conquered Scotland, and left in AD 410.

tf.s: The Romans conquered the whole of Britain, including Scotland.
The Romans built roads and public baths in Britain.
Julius Caesar successfully conquered Britain in 55 BC.
The Roman army left Britain in AD 410.
Hadrian's Wall was built to keep out the Picts.

explanation: The Anglo-Saxons came from northern Europe, and the Vikings arrived from Denmark and Norway in AD 789, later settling in the Danelaw.

tf.s: The Anglo-Saxons came to Britain from northern Europe.
The Vikings came to Britain from Spain and Portugal.
King Alfred the Great defeated the Vikings.
Sutton Hoo is the site of a Viking longhouse.
St Augustine became the first Archbishop of Canterbury.

explanation: William of Normandy defeated Harold at Hastings in 1066, ordered the Domesday Book in 1086, and the Normans built castles across England and Wales.

tf.s: The Battle of Hastings was fought in 1066.
Harold defeated William of Normandy at the Battle of Hastings.
The Domesday Book recorded who lived in the towns and villages of England.
The Norman Conquest was the last successful foreign invasion of England.
The Bayeux Tapestry commemorates the signing of Magna Carta.

explanation: Magna Carta was agreed in 1215, the Black Death arrived in 1348, and the Wars of the Roses ended at Bosworth Field in 1485.

tf.s: Magna Carta established that the king was subject to the law.
The Black Death killed about a third of the population of England.
The Wars of the Roses were fought between England and France.
Robert the Bruce defeated the English at Bannockburn in 1314.
The Hundred Years War lasted exactly one hundred years.
Geoffrey Chaucer wrote The Canterbury Tales.

explanation: Henry VIII had six wives and broke with Rome. Elizabeth I was Protestant and the Spanish Armada was defeated in 1588.

tf.s: Henry VIII had six wives.
Henry VIII established the Church of England.
The Spanish Armada defeated the English navy in 1588.
Elizabeth I never married and had no children.
Mary I was known as Bloody Mary because she persecuted Protestants.
Henry VII was the last Tudor monarch.

explanation: James VI of Scotland became James I of England in 1603. The Civil War began in 1642, Charles I was executed in 1649, and the monarchy was restored in 1660.

tf.s: James VI of Scotland became James I of England in 1603.
Charles I was executed in 1649.
Oliver Cromwell was crowned King of England.
The Great Fire of London took place in 1666.
The Glorious Revolution of 1688 involved a long and bloody war in England.
The Bill of Rights of 1689 limited the power of the monarch.

explanation: The Act of Union of 1707 created Great Britain, Walpole is regarded as the first Prime Minister, and Britain led the Industrial Revolution.

tf.s: The Act of Union of 1707 joined the English and Scottish parliaments.
Sir Robert Walpole is regarded as the first British Prime Minister.
The Battle of Culloden in 1746 was the last battle fought on British soil.
Admiral Nelson died at the Battle of Waterloo.
The Duke of Wellington defeated Napoleon at Waterloo in 1815.
Britain was the last country in Europe to industrialise.

explanation: Queen Victoria reigned from 1837 to 1901. Slavery was abolished across the Empire in 1833 and the Great Exhibition was held in 1851.

tf.s: Queen Victoria reigned for more than 60 years.
Slavery was abolished throughout the British Empire in 1833.
The Great Exhibition of 1851 was held in the Crystal Palace.
Florence Nightingale is considered the founder of modern nursing.
The Reform Act of 1832 gave women the right to vote.
The British Empire covered about a quarter of the world's population by 1913.

explanation: The First World War ended in 1918 and the Second World War ran from 1939 to 1945. The NHS was founded in 1948.

tf.s: The First World War ended at 11am on 11 November 1918.
The Second World War began in 1939.
Winston Churchill became Prime Minister in 1940.
The Battle of Britain was fought mainly at sea.
The NHS was established in 1948.
Women in Britain were given the vote on the same terms as men in 1928.
Margaret Thatcher was the UK's first female Prime Minister.

explanation: British discoveries include penicillin, radar, the jet engine, the hovercraft, television, the structure of DNA and the World Wide Web.

tf.s: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin.
Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web.
John Logie Baird invented the telephone.
Alan Turing worked on breaking German codes at Bletchley Park.
Dolly the sheep was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.
The world's first test-tube baby was born in the UK.

explanation: The UK voted to leave the European Union on 23 June 2016 by 51.9% to 48.1%, and formally left on 31 January 2020.

tf.s: The referendum on EU membership was held in 2016.
The UK formally left the European Union on 31 January 2020.
A majority voted to remain in the European Union in the 2016 referendum.
Scotland voted to become independent in the 2014 referendum.

explanation: The Church of England is the established Church in England and the Church of Scotland is Presbyterian. There is no established Church in Wales or Northern Ireland.

tf.s: The monarch is the head of the Church of England.
The Church of Scotland is a Roman Catholic Church.
There is an established Church in Wales.
Everyone in the UK has the right to change their religion or have none.
Some senior bishops of the Church of England sit in the House of Lords.

explanation: St George is the patron saint of England (23 April), St David of Wales (1 March), St Patrick of Northern Ireland (17 March) and St Andrew of Scotland (30 November).

tf.s: St Andrew is the patron saint of Scotland.
St David's Day is celebrated on 1 March.
St George is the patron saint of Wales.
St Patrick's Day falls on 17 March.
The patron saint's day is an official holiday in England.

explanation: Christmas is on 25 December, Boxing Day on 26 December, Bonfire Night on 5 November and Remembrance Day on 11 November.

tf.s: Boxing Day is celebrated on 26 December.
Bonfire Night remembers the Gunpowder Plot of 1605.
Halloween is a bank holiday in the UK.
Poppies are worn to mark Remembrance Day.
Lent lasts for 40 days before Easter.
Valentine's Day is celebrated on 14 February.
Hogmanay is the Welsh celebration of New Year.
Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan.
Diwali is celebrated by Hindus and Sikhs.

explanation: Football is the UK's most popular sport. Cricket and rugby originated in the UK, and Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament in the world.

tf.s: Football is the most popular sport in the UK.
Cricket originated in Australia.
The Ashes is contested between England and Australia.
Wimbledon is played on a grass surface.
St Andrews in Scotland is regarded as the home of golf.
London has hosted the Olympic Games three times.
The Grand National is a motor race.

explanation: Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon, the Proms is organised by the BBC, and the Turner Prize is awarded for contemporary art.

tf.s: William Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon.
The Proms is a season of classical music organised by the BBC.
The Turner Prize is awarded for popular music.
Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral.
Robert Burns is the national poet of Scotland.
The BAFTAs are awards for achievement in film and television.
Charles Dickens wrote Pride and Prejudice.

explanation: The Giant's Causeway is in Northern Ireland, Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales and Ben Nevis the highest in the UK.

tf.s: The Giant's Causeway is in Northern Ireland.
Snowdon is the highest mountain in the UK.
The Eden Project is in Cornwall.
The National Trust is a charity that preserves buildings and countryside.
Edinburgh Castle is built on an extinct volcano.
The Lake District is in Scotland.

explanation: The UK is a constitutional monarchy with an unwritten constitution. The monarch is Head of State and the Prime Minister is Head of Government.

tf.s: The UK constitution is contained in a single written document.
The monarch is the Head of State of the UK.
The monarch is expected to remain politically neutral.
There are 650 Members of Parliament in the House of Commons.
Members of the House of Lords are elected by the public.
The Speaker of the House of Commons must be politically neutral.
A general election must be held at least every five years.

explanation: The devolved administrations were established in 1999. Education and health are devolved, while defence and foreign affairs are reserved to the UK government.

tf.s: The Scottish Parliament sits at Holyrood in Edinburgh.
Defence is a devolved matter for Scotland and Wales.
Health services are devolved to Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
The Northern Ireland Assembly meets at Stormont.
The devolved administrations were established in 1999.

explanation: Juries have 12 members in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, and 15 in Scotland. Magistrates are unpaid and need no legal qualifications.

tf.s: A jury in England and Wales has 12 members.
A jury in Scotland has 15 members.
Magistrates must be qualified solicitors.
The police must obey the law themselves.
Scotland has its own separate legal system.
The Crown Court deals with the most serious criminal cases in England and Wales.
Discrimination on grounds of religion or race is legal in the UK.

explanation: You can vote at 18 if on the electoral register, voting is by secret ballot, and jury service is a civic duty.

tf.s: You must be on the electoral register in order to vote.
Voting in a UK election is by secret ballot.
Polling stations are open from 7am to 10pm on election day.
Serving on a jury when called is a civic duty.
You must be 21 to vote in a UK general election.
National Insurance contributions help fund the State Pension.
Driving without insurance is a criminal offence in the UK.

explanation: The UK is a permanent member of the UN Security Council, a member of NATO and of the Commonwealth, and of the Council of Europe.

tf.s: The UK is a permanent member of the UN Security Council.
The Commonwealth has legal power over its member states.
NATO members agree to help one another if attacked.
The Council of Europe drew up the European Convention on Human Rights.

section: The values and principles of the UK
explanation: The fundamental principles of British life are democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, tolerance of different faiths and beliefs, and participation in community life.

tf.s: Democracy is a fundamental principle of British life.
The rule of law means that those who govern are also subject to the law.
The UK tolerates extremism as a form of free expression.
Participation in community life is a fundamental principle of British life.
Everyone in the UK has the right to a fair trial.
Residents of the UK are expected to look after the area in which they live.

explanation: The UK is England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. Great Britain is England, Scotland and Wales only.

tf.s: The UK is made up of four countries.
Great Britain includes Northern Ireland.
The Isle of Man is a Crown dependency, not part of the UK.
Cardiff is the capital of Wales.
The currency of the UK is the euro.
Wales is represented on the Union Flag.
Northern Ireland shares a land border with the Republic of Ireland.
